EVENT_NARRATIVE: An F1 tornado touched down in McDougal. The tornado traveled approximately 14 miles before lifting into the clouds around St. Francis. One house in McDougal was destroyed and several others were damaged.

An F1 tornado touched down in the southeast part of Van Buren and traveled approximately 0.3 of a mile. Most of the damage consisted of one side and the roof of a storage warehouse being torn off. A trailer was overturned and several trees and power lines were also knocked down.
A weather spotter reported that the tornado touched down briefly near the intersection of Highway 99 and Chestnut Street.

A tornado touched down briefly in southern Denver, destroying a 4-inch thick concrete roof of a building, causing about $20,000 damage. The tornado also picked up a dumpster and dropped it onto a car 30 feet away, causing an estimated $3000. No injuries were reported.
A weather observer at the La Junta Municipal Airport reported a tornado north of Rocky Ford. The tornado was short-lived, but uprooted several large trees.
The county sheriff reported two separate short-lived tornadoes, one south of Flagler. Both touched down in open fields. No injuries or damage were reported.
The tornado northwest of Springfield touched down in an open field, with no damage reported. No injuries were reported.
The county sheriff reported a short-lived tornado southwest of Burlington. Touched down in an open field. No injuries or damage were reported.
County emergency manager reported a tornado touched down in an open field north of Cheyenne Wells. The tornado was short-lived, but uprooted several large trees. No injuries were reported.
Severe thunderstorms produced short-lived tornadoes near Walsh. The tornado near Walsh toppled power lines, causing about $5,000 damage.
A spotter reported a small tornado southwest of Holyoke. The tornado touched down in an open field, and was on the ground for a short time. No damage or injuries was reported.
Baca County Sheriff reported a brief tornado touch-down in an open field southwest of Springfield. No damage or injuries was reported.
The public reported a small tornado south of Lamar. The tornado touched down in an open field and was on the ground for about 10 minutes before dissipating. No injuries or damages were reported.
State patrol reported a brief tornado touchdown south of Eads. No injuries or damage was reported.

A weather spotter reported a brief tornado touch down southeast of Akron. He described it as a ground-based swirl of dust with no apparent connection to the base of the storm. No injuries or damage was reported.
A tornado was spotted by a sheriff's deputy northwest of Anton. The short-lived tornado touched down in an open field, with no damage or injuries reported.
A small, short-lived tornado blew a grain bin onto a combine, causing about $1,500 damage. No injuries were reported.
A waterspout was briefly observed along the south side of Ramrod Key.
A small tornado uprooted trees and cracked limbs near the Orange Tree subdivision in the northeast part of the county. (Coordinates from SPC modified by text/radar)
A second small tornado touched down along county road 846 doing minimal damage. (Coordinates from SPC modified by text/radar)
A small tornado uprooted trees as it moved across the Everglades in the west part of the county.
A small tornado moved through River Trails Trailer Park destroying one trailer and damaging nine others.
A citizen reported a tornado briefly on the ground south of Lake Panasoffkee. Trees and power lines were blown over.

A tornado touched down at Clearwater-Largo Road downing trees and power lines (F0 damage). It lifted and moved west one-half mile before touching down again in Belleair moving through an industrial area. A car and a sailboat were flipped over. Six doors were blown out of storage units. Windows were broken out. Tops of trees and large limbs were twisted and broken off (F1 damage). The tornado then lifted again moved southwest and set down again over the Belleair Causeway. It then moved over the bay and dissipated.

Two waterspouts were observed 5 miles north of Key West.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A waterspout was observed 5 miles north of the Marathon airport.
A tornado touched down in a residential area near downtown where it tore off some house shingles. It moved to Tampa Bay before dissipating.
A tornado touched down in Bradenton blowing down a fence and downing a tree.
A waterspout was observed 5 miles south of Key West.
A small tornado damaged a house roof in Jacksonville.
A small tornado scattered backyard furniture in LaBelle.
A waterspout was observed 4 miles north of Key West.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A waterspout was observed 6 miles west of the Key West airport.
A waterspout was observed just off the Lake Worth Inlet.
A waterspout was observed 2 miles north of the Key West airport.

A waterspout formed over Newfound Harbor and moved northwest onshore at Merritt Island airport. It overturned three single engine aircraft and destroyed eight ultralights. It then moved into an industrial area where it blew over a few trees and destroyed a warehouse roof before disappearing in the Indian River.
A small tornado moved across Siesta Key ripping sheet metal roofing from a building. A car window was knocked out by flying debris.
A small tornado struck Crescent Beach uprooting trees and peeling roofing off a storage shed and two houses. Golf carts being kept in the storage shed were also damaged.
A waterspout was observed 2 miles east of Melbourne.
A tornado was observed by law enforcement officials in southwest Dade County. Debris was observed rotating and falling in the area.
A short lived tornado touched down and destroyed a mobile home, several garages, a few barns and downed several trees along its path.

One mobile home was destroyed and another severely damaged by a short lived tornado. The severely damaged mobile home was shifted off its foundation several inches and commodes were torn out of the bathroom. A corn auger and water storage tank were turned over by the tornado while a vehicle was damaged from wind blown debris.

A short lived tornado touched near the intersection of U.S. Highway 17 and Georgia Highway 303. The tornado twisted off the tops of several large pine trees and removed a roof from a small building along its path.
A short lived and weak tornado touched down near the eastern banks of the Chattahoochee River and skipped east with little damage. A few trees were twisted off at the crowns.

A tornado, which formed at a location 14 miles south of Pocatello, skipped along a 10-mile-long path to the northeast, ending in Inkom, 13 miles southeast of Pocatello. The tornado did significant damage. Dozens of trees were uprooted and twisted. The tornado knocked over a grain elevator and overturned a semi truck. Several outbuildings were destroyed and numerous windows were broken out of buildings. Two minor injuries were reported, both attributed to falling limbs. An inspection of the storm site was completed by National Weather Service Personnel. This inspection revealed this tornado to be an F1 scale tornado based on the damage sustained. EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two tornadoes, 50 miles northwest of Idaho Falls, were spotted by a U.S. Forest Service employee. Some damage was done to the metal roof of a trailer house. Another tornado, 35 miles northwest of Idaho Falls also caused minor damage to trees. Four funnel clouds accompanied the latter tornado.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A severe weather spotter reported a tornado 55 miles northwest of Idaho Falls. The tornado was on the ground for two minutes, then ascended and was visible as a funnel for another 30 minutes. No damage was reported.

A small tornado touched down several times along the path damaging the roofs of five homes as well as minor roof damage to several other homes. Also, numerous large trees and power lines were blown down.
A small tornado touched down several times damaging part of a school and destroyed 5 large storage facilities and 4 garages, and damaged 63 homes. Four homes and one apartment were uninhabitable.
A tornado touched down briefly just north of town tearing down power lines and trees. Two local farmers witnessed the touchdown but no injuries were reported.

A tornado destroyed an empty mobile home and laundrymat. Numerous windows were broken in homes and many trees were blown down. There was minor damage to some roofs and a shed was destroyed. Damage was estimated around $250,000.
A tornado briefly touched down north of the junction of Route 150 and Staley Road.
Another tornado touched down briefly north of Champaign causing roof damage to a house and a barn.
A tornado touched down briefly near Interstate 74 causing no damage.
A tornado tore off part of the roof of an office building and blew down some large tree limbs and power lines
Another tornado touched down east of Danville near Interstate 74.
A mini-tornado was spotted touching down briefly at route 176 and 47 near Crystal Lake.

A small tornado that touched down briefly in Sterling, Illinois. A car full of people sighted the tornado on Illinois State Route 2 and the corner of Woodlawn Road. Damage consisted of twisted trees, light poles, and a large swing set destroyed.
A tornado was spotted over the Ohio River. It lifted before reaching land.

An F3 tornado touched down in Iowa. It crossed the Mississippi River into Illinois at 1602 CST and crossed into Wisconsin at 1612 CST. It weakened to F1 intensity and had a skipping path over northwest Jo Daviess County. Minor damage to trees and outbuildings occurred at a farm near Menominee.
State Police reported a tornado on the ground in a rural area near town.
State Police reported a brief touchdown.
A small tornado was witnessed touching down briefly in Pittsfield. It knocked down one tree and damaged a few others at the courthouse. Windows were blown in at a store in town.
A small tornado touched down briefly at the Illinois-Wisconsin state line at Route 14. An office trailer was damaged.

The tornado destroyed a mobile home near the initial touchdown site, and injured a man who was inside asleep when it hit. The tornado also downed trees, damaged or destroyed several barns and farm buildings, and toppled chimneys and ripped siding from houses.
A tornado briefly touched down, and uprooted several trees and downed power lines.

A tornado produced a short and narrow damage path through Elrod. Many outbuildings, barns, and mobile homes were destroyed. Many houses and businesses were severely damaged. A large fuel tank weighing several tons was moved about 100 yards. Four of the six injuries occurred inside a mobile home.
A waterspout was reported at Indiana Harbor.
A small tornado briefly touched down, but caused no damage.
The path of the tornado was intermittent, with only sporadic damage noted. The tornado downed trees and telephone poles, and ripped the roof from a barn.

The path of the tornado was intermittent. Numerous trees and power lines were downed, the roof was blown from a barn, and the roof of a silo was blown off. There was extensive damage at the Shady Lane Campground and Mobile Home Park southwest of Plymouth. At this location one mobile home was crushed by a falling tree, and at least two cars were damaged by falling trees. The roof was also blown from a house near Plymouth. Total damage was estimated between $90,000 and $100,000.
A small tornado briefly touched down.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As the low mentioned above continued to move northeast, the warm front pressed into Iowa and a dry line moved across the plains. Thunderstorms fired ahead of the dry line in northwest Iowa. The storms fired from a combination of the dry line and synoptic forcing. The first storms produced a 65 mph wind gust near Arnolds Park. The winds lifted boats from their moorings and overturned a couple of them. Several tornadoes were spawned by the storms. The strongest was in Lyon and Osceola Counties. The tornado was on the ground for about 10 miles. Though much of its path was over open country, the tornado did cause significant damage in Sibley. On its path, the tornado destroyed a cattle shed, blew out windows, and downed several trees. In Sibley, one roof was taken off of a house and a high school bus barn was taken down. Damage to the bus barn was around $150,000. There were several injuries in Sibley caused by flying glass and debris. Two other were injured as the collided while driving their cars in an attempt to outrun the tornado. Ironically, the call to action statement in the tornado warning for the area specifically advised NOT to try to outrun the tornado in your car. A second tornado was on the ground for about 7.5 miles. This tornado was not as strong, but did cause damage in Sioux County between Hospers and Sheldon. Several barns were taken down, along with a few silos. The tornado moved into the campus of the Northwest Iowa Community College, causing quite a bit of damage to the buildings. Other tornadoes touched down in the area in what turned out to be a small family of tornadoes. Damage was minor as the other tornadoes swept across open countryside. Lightning struck a house in Milford, starting a small fire.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: The storms touched off a brief tornado touch down in Boone County. During its brief life, one house was damage in the town of Fraser.
Another tornado touched down briefly at the Forest City Airport. A few buildings were damaged by this tornado.

A tornado was spawned by the storm southeast of the Osage area. Fortunately, it tracked across farm fields for the most part. It did strike four farmsteads, damaging one severely. Several small out buildings and barns were damaged but the farm houses were spared. On one farmstead, a pine tree was picked up and thrown over the house. A car was lifted and thrown 70 meters. Several calves and one pig were killed.
South of this area, a small tornado touched down north of Wyman. It was on the ground for about 5 miles.
One tornado occurred in the southwest part of Iowa northeast of Red Oak. Little damage occurred as the tornado crossed open country, though it did take one trailer off of its foundation.
A tornado touched down briefly in Wright County south of the Clarion Airport. Witnesses reported seeing the tornado pick up dirt as it touched down in an open field.

One barn was destroyed, however the hogs in the barn were able to escape. The tornado toppled over head stones in a cemetery southwest of Sigourney. The tornado briefly lifted as it crossed highway 149, then touched down and destroyed two out buildings and tore the side off an airplane hanger at the Sigourney Airport. Extensive damage was reported at the airport.

A strong tornado touched down in Delaware County. The storm was tracked by weather radar as a mesocyclone. It touched down south and west of Manchester, causing major structural damage to a farm house. Later it picked up a car, spun it around, and turned it upside down north of Manchester. It moved into a forested area and finally lifted.

The third tornado was also quite strong. It touched down south of the Dubuque Airport. Tree branches fell out of the sky onto the runway at the Dubuque Airport. A large piece of sheet metal fell on top of the terminal building. A Northwest Airlink flight landed at the airport with tree branches attached to the aircraft. At least one farmstead was hit with a glancing blow. About $15,000 damage was reported with several propane tanks leaking following the damage caused by the tornado. The tornado tracked north-northeast across the extreme northwest tip of Illinois and into southwest Wisconsin where it finally dissipated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several tornadoes were spawned during the evening. Most of them were brief touch downs and caused little damage. Such was the case in Greene County, where two brief touch downs occurred in open countryside. An earlier touch down north of Sibley, in Ocseola County, did little more than cause tree damage. Two tornadoes touched down in Pocahontas County. The first was a brief touch down. The second was on the ground between Havelock and Gilmore City. Much of the area it traversed was open country. A few farmsteads were affected with most damage to out buildings. One farmstead received significant damage northwest of Gilmore City just before the tornado lifted. The storm was still strong as it moved across the city. Damage was substantial at a lumber yard as high winds lifted the roof from the building and threw it into a house across the street. The lumber yard building was virtually destroyed it. The longest tornado track cut across three counties. The tornado touched down in Boone County and cut a path across southern Story County into northeast Polk County. This tornado had a very intermittent track and lifted several times or remained just above ground. As it moved across northeast Polk County, the storm weakened. Damage was limited due to its intermittent track and the fact that that part of the state is not heavily populated. The storm moved into Jasper County, but by then was below severe levels and just produced heavy rainfall and some small hail. During the late night hours, two tornadoes touched down in Scott County. One north of New Liberty was only a brief touch down and caused no significant damage. The second was north of the Stockton area. A couple was camping in Scott County north of Stockton. The tornado rolled their mobile home. The husband received several cuts and bruises. His wife sustained a broken arm and cuts that required 24 stitches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An earlier touch down north of Sibley, in Ocseola County, did little more than cause tree damage.

The tornado touched down in Boone County and cut a path across southern Story County into northeast Polk County. This tornado had a very intermittent track and lifted several times or remained just above ground. As it moved across northeast Polk County, the storm weakened. Damage was limited due to its intermittent track and the fact that that part of the state is not heavily populated. The storm moved into Jasper County, but by then was below severe levels and just produced heavy rainfall and some small hail. During the late night hours, two tornadoes touched down in Scott County. One north of New Liberty was only a brief touch down and caused no significant damage. The second was north of the Stockton area. A couple was camping in Scott County north of Stockton. The tornado rolled their mobile home. The husband received several cuts and bruises. His wife sustained a broken arm and cuts that required 24 stitches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Most of them were brief touch downs and caused little damage. Such was the case in Greene County, where two brief touch downs occurred in open countryside.

Tornado lasted 5 minutes moving to the southeast at over 20 mph over open country.
A brief tornado was moving southeast over open country.

In Sumner County 20 square miles, or about 10,000 acres, of wheat were damaged by a hail storm... The storm also spawned a brief tornado that touched down in a park on the southeast side of Wellington, but there was no danage.
Storm watchers reported a brief tornado hit in an open field. A well defined rotating wall cloud and several funnels were also visible as the storm moved southeast.
This tornado touched down over open country and remained over open country until it dissipated.
This tornado touched down over open country, blew the siding off of a steel shed at one farmstead, and dissipated shortly thereafter.
This tornado touched down over open country, then destroyed the roof of a barn before dissipating.

A lone thunderstorm developed in front of a line of thunderstorms. A tornado was reported by the public in open farmland. This tornado touched down briefly. The thunderstorm that produced this tornado continued to move to the east.
Tornado moved 10 mph east-southeast over open country.
A brief tornado was reported over open country.
A tornado moved south at 40 mph.
A brief tornado was reported over open country.

Many roofs to homes and mobile homes were damaged or destroyed on the east side of Garden City. Two mobile homes were knocked off their foundations. A semi trailer truck was knocked over. Six hanger doors at the Garden City Airport were blown off. One hangar door was blown into a Aerostar airplane parked inside the hangar. A modular classroom at Victor Ornlelas Elementary School was knocked off its foundation.
A weak, short-lived tornado touched down on the Fort Riley firing range area causing no damage.
A tornado hit briefly in an open field causing no damage.

A tornado destroyed two farmsteads and damaged several others along with several adjacent outbuildings, sheds and machinery... A man rode out the tornado in the cab of a pickup truck that was parked in shed that was demolished by the tornado.

The same supercell thunderstorm that produced a tornado near Keats dropped another weak tornado in the Hunters Island area south of Manhattan. Substantial damage occurred to about six or eight homes and buildings.
Another weak tornado dropped from the slow moving supercell and hit along Deep Creek east of Highway K177. Only minor damage was noted.
A weak tornado briefly hit in an open field.
A small tornado was reported at Oak Level (16 miles southeast of Paducah). Structural damage to homes and some small businesses was reported. Numerous trees and power lines were also blown down.
A tornado briefly touched down about 1 mile south of Visalia. Large trees were uprooted and some small outbuildings were damaged.
A small tornado touched down in the Cold Hill area of London. Several homes were damaged and many trees and power lines were blown down.
A small tornado touched down near Bagdad. No damage was reported.
A small tornado touched down in the northeast part of the county.
A small tornado touched down in the central portion of the county. Only trees and power lines were blown down.
A small, brief tornado destroyed a 600 pound kennel fence about 0.25 miles southeast of the Lake Charles National Weather Service Office.
A waterspout-tornado on an intermittent path made landfall in Metairie where it damaged trees and the roofs of about 13 homes.

A tornado made a brief touchdown... damaging an industrial building. The front wall of the building was destroyed and a huge exhaust fan vent was torn from the roof... damage at the industrial site was estimated at $75,000.

A F0 tornado moved through the Sterling Heights area... Pieces of steel plating from Bond robotics were moved from their original location... Scaffolding fell and was twisted. A 3-inch-diameter limb was driven into the ground.

A tornado traveled along an intermittent path damaging a meat processing plant on the west side of Luverne and damaged several homes in the city of Luverne. As it moved northeast... the tornado damaged several buildings on area farms.

A tornado struck southwest of Tracy damaging a farmstead. It traveled into Tracy and severely damaged 17 mobile homes in a mobile home court. The local high school received nearly $140,000 damage and a total of six people sustained injuries.
A small tornado struck downtown sections of Canby damaging several buildings and felling a number of trees.
A tornado damaged several homes and other buildings around Seaforth.
A short lived tornado touched down briefly on the south end of Lakefield damaging a few buildings.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Three tornado briefly touched down across Mower County and did not cause any damage.
Three tornado briefly touched down across Mower County and did not cause any damage.
Three tornado briefly touched down across Mower County and did not cause any damage.
Two tornados touched down briefly across Fillmore County and did not cause damage.
Two tornados touched down briefly across Fillmore County and did not cause damage.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tornado touched down briefly and dissipated doing no damage.
A tornado touched down briefly on the northeast side of Little Jessie Lake damaging the roof of a resort and blowing down as many as 30 trees.
A tornado touched down briefly near Dover and did not cause damage.
A tornado touched down briefly without causing damage.
A tornado touched down briefly near Mizpah and did no damage.
A tornado touched down briefly and dissipated near the town of Bagely.
A tornado touched down briefly near Nielsville.
A small tornado touched down 25 miles northeast of Poplar Bluff. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down. Reported by the county sheriff.

County officials reported a tornado that tracked from near Sturdivant to just south of Advance. In Bollinger County, a mobile home and farm house were destroyed, along with structural damage to other homes. Many trees and power lines were knocked down along the tornado path.

A spotter reported a tornado touch down briefly at her farm. Two windows were pulled out of her house and the barn roof was lifted up but not torn off. Two trees were broken off near their tops and an outbuilding was destroyed. Two large haystacks were also flattened and scattered about.
A tornado touched down briefly in rural Worth damaging several shed roofs and demolishing a barn. Time estimated from local newspaper reports.

The county EOC reported a tornado touchdown along Highway CC between Racine and Highway 60. A large oak tree fell damaging two cars and a house along Highway CC. One person received minor cuts from flying glass when the storm broke windows out. A nearby mobile home was also damaged while numerous trees were knocked down along the path.
A tornado touched down briefly but there were no reports of damage.
A tornado touched down briefly in the eastern sections of Maryville, but no damage was reported.
A brief touchdown was reported.
A tornado touched down briefly but there were no reports of damage.
A brief touchdown knocked down large trees but no other damage was reported.
A tornado touched down in extreme northwest Ralls County. Two homes sustained damage to their roofs and another had siding damage. Barns near the homes were also heavily damaged.
A small tornado touched down briefly southwest of Hannibal in a field. Only crop damage was sustained.
A tornado touched down briefly just southwest of Palmyra. The Hannibal EOC said the tornado crossed Highway 36 but no damage was reported.
A tornado briefly touched down 0.5 mile west of the airport. Four mobile homes were damaged.
A spotter on Hauser Lake saw a waterspout come ashore and overturned some picnic tables.
A tornado touched down on the Meadowlark Golf Course and destroyed a tree and damaged the club house. A car dealership on the east end of Great Falls received damage.

Multiple tornados formed in west central Phelps county and southeast Dawson Counties... The tornado moved north across the southeast corner of Dawson County near Overton... before moving into western Buffalo County and striking Amherst. This tornado was nearly stationary in the Amherst area for almost 90 minutes. Five funnels were noted with this storm. It moved east northeast across Buffalo County to Ravenna, then into southeast Sherman County, and finally into Howard County near Boelus and Dannebrog. Ninety-seven homes were damaged, and three destroyed. Two children received cuts from flying glass as their home was destroyed at Ravenna.
A tornado was spotted in the southwest corner of Buffalo County near Elm Creek. The tornado moved northeast and was last seen near Amherst.

A tornado formed just south of Riverdale in western Buffalo County, moved east, passing north of Kearney and lifted six miles northwest of Shelton. It lifted as it passed over northwest Hall County, but dropped back down just west of St. Libory in southeast Howard County. This tornado moved at 5 to 10 mph.
A tornado was spotted just east of Overton or 5 miles west of Elm Creek. This tornado moved northeast and was last seen just southwest of Amherst.

A small tornado moved through the community knocking down tree limbs and a few trees. Some damage was also reported to games and rides of a carnival which were set up on city street for a local celebration.
A tornado briefly touched down near Clarks.
A tornado briefly touched down west of St. Libory. Funnel clouds were observed over the town.
A tornado briefly touched down in the extreme northwest corner of Perkins County.
A tornado was spotted 8 miles north of the Grand Island Airport in the southeast corner of Howard County.
A tornado was seen from the weather service office at the Grand Island Airport.
A tornado briefly touched down on a farm, tearing off tree tops and knocking down power lines. Golfball-size hail fell just ahead of the tornado.
A tornado briefly touched down north of Phillips.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Three or four funnel clouds were reported and two tornados touched down south and southeast of Bridgeport. One tornado tore out 100 yards of fence and upset an irrigation system. Another tornado uprooted more than 100 pine trees.

Three or four funnel clouds were reported and two tornados touched down south and southeast of Bridgeport. One tornado tore out 100 yards of fence and upset an irrigation system. Another tornado uprooted more than 100 pine trees.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tornado touched down in an open field with no damage.
A tornado damaged tree limbs before dissipating.
A tornado briefly touched down in open country. Spotters reported no damage.
A tornado touched down briefly at Chappell. Golfball-size hail was also reported.
A NWS employee spotted a tornado near Chappell. The tornado was short lived and caused no apparent damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Spotters reported a brief tornado west of Big Springs. Another tornado touched down briefly north of Big Springs from the same thunderstorm.
Spotters reported a brief tornado west of Big Springs. Another tornado touched down briefly north of Big Springs from the same thunderstorm.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tornado was spotted north of Alliance. The tornado destroyed a pump house.
A tornado briefly touched down near Arcadia.
A tornado was spotted just south of Cushing moving northeast. Heavy crop damage was noted just east of Cushing.
A tornado moving south left an intermittent path in open country. Power lines were knocked down 8 miles south of Broken Bow.
A tornado briefly touched down just west of Rockville.
In Piscataway a tornado touched down briefly, but no injuries were reported.
At Califon, in Hunterdon County, a tornado touched down briefly but no injuries were reported.
A tornado touched down briefly just north of Clovis at 1515 MST. It destroyed a small shed constructed of wood and tin.
Thunderstorms accompanied a cold front which crossed the area. The thunderstorms downed trees and power lines and spawned two small tornados.
Thunderstorms accompanied a cold front which crossed the area. The thunderstorms downed trees and power lines and spawned two small tornados.
A small tornado touched down in Potsdam uprooting trees, destroying a satellite dish and a large wooden jungle gym.

A tornado touched down in Pulteney in Steuben County around 1900 EDT. The tornado first touched down and damaged a garage, trailer and porch and moved a grill and picnic table about 100 feet... The tornado lifted off the ground and touched down again in a wooded area. There was considerable tree damage in this area with most of the trees broken about a third of the way up. The tornado lifted again and on its final touchdown appeared to do the most damage. The siding and gutters were torn off a house and a motor boat was picked off its trailer and moved about 20 feet. A trailer also suffered substantial damage and a large wooden shed was badly damaged. A large tractor inside the shed was moved about 10 feet. A husband and wife were injured by flying debris as they unsuccessfully attempted to reach a storm cellar under the barn.
A small tornado cut a narrow path through woods near Kerr Lake and caused minor damage to a cottage.

A tornado touched down near Highway 258 and skipped along the ground or at treetop level 5 miles to just south of Coakley. One mobile home and a packing house were destroyed. Another mobile home and a house were damaged.
A tornado was sighted 7 miles south of Rolla. The tornado crossed into Towner County where it destroyed a barn.
A tornado picked up farm equipment and deposited it in a shelter belt.
A brief tornado touchdown 4 miles west of Wing destroyed sections of fence.
A brief tornado touchdown blew out windows and tipped a wagon.
A tornado briefly touched down and was spotted by the sheriff. Trees were downed, several on homes. A metal grain bin collapsed and a roof was stripped from a house. Utility poles were downed.
A member of the McComb Fire Department witnessed the tornado touch down. Trees were downed and a barn destroyed in the mostly rural area.

A small tornado touched down near Lees Creek and moved southeast into Highland County at about 1356 EST. The tornado, which was witnessed and filmed by a citizen, was not on the ground the entire pathlength, and moved through a rural area. Trees were downed and minor damage occurred to a home and several outbuildings.

A small tornado touched down near Palestine-Hollansburg Road (between Palestine and Hollansburg) and a large section of roof was removed from a barn. The tornado proceeded east and touched down two more times but was on the ground no more than 40 yards at any one time. Trees were downed at the next touchdown 2 miles to the east. At the last touchdown at Clarks Station Road and Byrket a large well-constructed barn was destroyed and debris was scattered 0.25 mile.

A small tornado touched down 1 mile east of Pitsburg. The tornado skipped along to the southeast, only touching the ground every mile or so and being on the ground no more than 0.25 mile at any one time. The funnel crossed into southwestern Miami County at 1352 EST. A touchdown then occurred 2 miles southwest of Laura on State Route 721 and again 1 mile southeast of Ditmer Road and again 2 miles southeast of Shiloh Road. Trees were downed and one residence had a roof partially removed. The final touchdown at Potsdam-Milton Road resulted in a well-constructed barn being destroyed; very little debris was left at the site.
A tornado briefly touched down and damaged roofs of two adjacent homes.
A tornado briefly touched down just south of Martinsville near Jonesboro Road. Trees were downed, some on power lines.
A tornado touched down just north of Wilmington on Hilling Road. Trees were downed, some on power lines. A corn crib was damaged and windows were blown out of a house.
A tornado touched down briefly near Antioch Road almost on the Highland County line. Trees were downed, some on power lines.
A tornado touched down just inside the Highland County line (adjacent to Clinton County) and moved across an open field before dissipating.

A tornado touched down just northwest of Hillsboro and moved southeast skipping along a discontinuous path. Trees were downed but significant damage occurred near the end of the path around Belfast where one house was destroyed and several others severely damaged. Cars were rolled up to 100 yards and several high tension utility towers were destroyed. Witnesses in the area noted that several "smaller" tornadoes seemed to wrap around the main tornado. A mother and her child were injured falling down the basement stairs as the storm struck. A local man working in his barn on State Route 73 injured as winds destroyed the structure.

A tornado touched down near the Brown County border just east of State Route 136 and moved southeast along a discontinuous path. It remained north of the city of Winchester and dissipated near State Route 32. The tornado was briefly on the ground three seperate times. Trees and utility poles were downed. One barn was destroyed and several were damaged. Several homes received minor damage.

A tornado touched down in northeast Adams County near the Pike County border along State Route 73. The tornado skipped along a discontinuous path to the southeast touching down briefly six times. Trees and untility poles were downed. Two barns were destroyed and one home received minor damage.

A tornado touched down in northwest Scioto County near the town of Rarden along State Route 73. The tornado moved southeast and touched down only briefly twice. Trees were downed, some on power lines. Minor damage occurred to a utility barn at a state forest facility.

A tornado touched down in near Pike County on the Jefferson-Madison Township line and skipped southeast along a discontinuous path touching down briefly four times. One mobile home was destroyed and two other homes were damaged. Trees and utility poles were downed.
A tornado briefly touched down twice downing trrees and pulling one utility pole out of the ground.
A small tornado briefly touched down 4 miles north of Turpin at 2130 CST. No damage was reported from this F0 tornado.

A weak tornado developed .5 miles west of Overbrook at 0908 CST and traveled 1.5 miles before dissipating 1.5 miles east-northeast of Overbrook at 0913 CST. This F0 tornado damaged a horse barn, ripped metal from another barn, knocked out windows and broke off tree limbs.
A small tornado briefly touched down at 1607 CST in an open field 7 miles north of Blackwell. There was no damage associated with this F0 tornado.
Another F0 tornado touched down briefly at 1620 CST 4 miles northwest of Newkirk.

A strong tornado developed 3 miles south-southwest of Newkirk at 1635 CST and moved east-northeast 11.5 miles before dissipating at 1702 CST 10 miles east of Newkirk. This F3 tornado destroyed a two-story, five-bedroom brick house, a mobile home, three barns, a television tower, two out buildings, a motor home, a pop-up camper, a pole barn and a pole shed. The tornado downed trees and power lines and was between 100 and 250 yards wide.

Another tornado developed at 1715 CST approximately 14 miles east-southeast at Newkirk and moved east around 0.3 miles before dissipating at 1717 CST. This F0 tornado broke off tree limbs and downed trees.
The 3rd weak tornado developed at 1835 CST 1 mile south of Copan near U.S. Highway 75. No damage occurred as a result of this F0 tornado.

The first tornado briefly touched down at 1558 CST near the intersection of U.S. Highway 75 and 141st Street South in Glenpool. The tornado damaged a lumber yard and 2 or 3 mobile homes in this area before lifting. Damage to the lumber yard was estimated at $150,000. The manager of the lumber yard sustained a broken hand. This tornado was rated F0 in intensity.

The second tornado touched down at 1600 CST 4 miles north northeast of Sapulpa. The tornado damaged a house, garage and trees on the north side of Interstate 44 before crossing the interstate and damaging a truck driving school. The tornado moved east into Tulsa County at 1605 CST and damaged several homes and one apartment near 61st Street South and 33rd West Avenue. Several vehicles were also damaged in this area. The tornado lifted at 1606 CST near the intersection of U.S. Highway 75 and 61st Street South. The 3-mile-long and 50-yard-wide damage path was not continuous, and the tornado produced F0 to occasional F1 damage.

The third tornado touched down at 1615 CST near the intersection of Kent and Lyons Streets in Broken Arrow. The tornado caused considerable damage to several homes in this area. This 50-yard-wide tornado was on the ground for less than 1/8 mile and produced F0 to F1 damage.
The fourth tornado touched down very briefly near Oneta at 1619 CST. This F0 tornado uprooted trees.
Weak tornadoes formed just north of Lovell at 1625 CST. This F0 tornado developed over open fields and no damage was reported.
Weak tornadoes formed... 3 miles north-northwest of Crescent at 1650 CST [sic: table says 1647-. This F0 tornado developed over open fields and no damage was reported.

The length and width of this tornado were unknown and the intensity was determined from the damage reports. At 1833 EST several trees and wires were blown down and a car overturned in Windsor and lower Windsor townships. At 1845 EST, a roof was torn off a barn, and there was a partial road collapse of Snyder's Corner and Spring Hollow. In Locust Grove between Manor and Old Commons road, several mobile homes lost roofs.

A distinct path of damage was noted from the St. Josephs Cemetery to just east of the community of Coupon. One resident said he saw trees flying through the air, with one tree flying right over the top of his house. A total of twenty residences were damaged. One swimming pool and a small shed were completely destroyed.

From Everson to Wooddale, a tornado destroyed 3 mobile homes and two barns. One of the mobile homes overturned and injured a 45-year-old women. The second mobile home the roof tore off, which landed into a nearby fire station causing $20,000 in damage to the Bullskin Township fire station. A firemen at the station was injured by flying debris. Siding was torn from several other homes, and a porch roof was ripped from a house. A total of 23 homes, 9 mobile homes, 3 barns, a private school, and 1 business received minor damage. Along Route 1047, east of Scottdale, a 1,000 pound horse was seen flying through the air before landing in a nearby creek. The horse underwent surgery for an 8-inch gash to the chest. Five other horses were also fifted off the ground, and carried several hundred yards.

This small and short-lived tornado was first spotted near North Brandywine JHS and travelled southeast crossing route 30. The tornado veered southwest after crossing route 340 and dissipated in an area east of the Veterans Administration Medical Center. A funnel cloud was spotted aloft during a large portion of the route. The hardest hit area was apparently near Caln. Crews worked through the night to clear dozens of trees and branches, tangled wires, replace fallen utility poles and repair damaged transformers. The hospital was forced to us emergency generator power. Just down the road from the hospital, a barn built in 1812 was turned to rubble. The tornado pushed the silo about 6 inches off its base and collapsed the roof, crushing farm equipment inside. Newly planted crops were blown in all directions and there were 7,000 power outages throughout the county. An AT&T employee was killed when a falling tree struck his vehicle as he was driving north on North Caln Road about 1530 EST. The tree also snapped two electric wires on the way down, preventing rescue workers from getting to the man. (M45V)

Trees were uprooted, broken and twisted off in all directions. The damage was on top of a hill. An eye witness saw the tornado tear up the trees after heavy rain and half dollar-size hail had moved through the area.
Tornado of waterspout origin came from inlet side and tore off or damaged roofs of four homes. Furnishings were smashed against walls and furniture was strewn about by the winds.

A tornado extensively damaged one farm northeast of Kimball and caused damage to other farms. Several children riding their bicycles in Kimball were picked up by the winds and thrown to the ground causing minor injury.
A tornado ripped out trees and power lines.

A large tornado on the ground for at least 10 minutes destroyed a farmstead. The tornado twisted the house on its foundation virtually destroying it, and destroyed the barn, 3 steel bins, 3 granaries, and 2 hog houses. Ten hogs were also killed. Trees were uprooted and twisted up to a mile north of the farm and pieces of tin roof were wrapped around trees 0.25 mile from the farm.

A large tornado and its attendant vortices left a swath of destruction from northwest Minnehaha County through western Moody County into eastern Brookings County. Numerous farms and residences were destroyed or damaged and trees snapped off or uprooted. Around 1630 CDT multiple vortices formed into the tornado two miles west of Lyons destroying barns and silos and killing animals on several farms. Shortly after, the tornado leveled two houses, seriously injuring four people as they were buried in the rubble. It then caused destruction on at least 10 more farms before entering the northwest side of Colman at 1700 CDT. At least 15 homes in Colman had an estimated total of $250,000 in damage mainly due to the roofs either being blown off or trees falling on them. At 1710 CDT the tornado damaged houses and trees three miles north/northeast of Colman. Around 1715 CDT, 10 miles northwest of Flandreau, the tornado leveled a farm, except for the silo, and injured a man who received multiple pelvis fractures. On two farms, one 2 miles southwest of Aurora and the other 1 mile west of Aurora, buildings and grain bins were destroyed around 1735 CDT. The tornado then continued north/northeast, wrecking irrigation systems and uprooting and snapping off hundreds of trees, before causing destruction on another farm about 6 miles northeast of Brookings around 1745 CDT. Northeast of White, three farms sustained major damage to buildings and trees. Cows were also killed and power lines downed.

A large tornado tore a north/northeast path of destruction through at least 10 farms. On one farm southeast of Junius all that remained was the foundation and steps of the house and the bumper and engine of a pickup truck. On other farms livestock were crippled and a horse was impaled by a piece of wood. At least four people were injured as several vehicles were flipped by the tornado. A woman was driving on a highway west of Madison when the wind started spinning her car around and the windows shattered. About 200 power poles were downed leaving 2800 customers without electricity.

The heavy rain forced the closure of State Highway 61 south of Otis. Thunderstorm winds leveled a cattle shed south of Briggsdale (24 miles northeast of Greeley).

Numerous big trees were knocked down by a downburst that was just over two miles long and about eight-tenths of a mile wide and probably had an embedded FO tornado within the downburst. Many branches were torn off. Debris was in piles, a few windows were broken and the storm was accompanied by ping-pong-size hail that covered the ground to a depth of two inches in spots. Funnel cloud sightings were called to the Chaplin town dispatcher. The lay out of the damage suggested a tornado did occur but was probably on the ground only momentarily.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The Illinois State Police reported seeing funnel clouds near Mason with reports of unconfirmed tornado touchdowns. This same storm produced a confirmed brief touchdown near Watson. The tornado was sighted by a state trooper and two citizens touching down in an open field. No damage was reported.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Numerous buildings and homes sustained roof damage. Trees and signs were blown down. A grain elevator was blown over. At least 12 utility poles were knocked down. The most severe damage was to a three story apartment building. The wall of the top floor was blown in and the roof collapsed.

The back of a salt storage silo was blown off by small tornado. State police reported that the tornado touched down at mile marker 91 on Interstate 39 near Interstate 88. Two cars were damaged by flying debris.

The tornado destroyed two mobile homes, and damaged a house and barn. A man who was inside one of the mobile homes that was destroyed was seriously injured. The tornado also downed numerous trees and power lines.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough was moving through the area during the late afternoon hours. Most of the thunderstorm activity associated with this feature remained to the north of Iowa. The southern extension of the area brushed northwest Iowa. There were two reports of severe weather. A small tornado touched down briefly in a field south of George in Lyon County. Hail the size of nickels fell south of Ashton in Osceola County.

A warm frontal boundary was to the south of Iowa during the afternoon. During the afternoon hours, moisture was transported over the top of the boundary while heating destabilized the atmosphere over the state. Funnel clouds were reported in the central and east central counties. Intense thunderstorms erupted over the east central counties, however only one produced severe weather in central Iowa, and a second in the east central counties. A tornado touched down in Poweshiek County along Interstate 80. The tornado moved across fields as it paralleled the Interstate. It lifted, though the funnel remained for a while, with no significant damage reported. Funnel clouds were also reported over east central Iowa. One brief touchdown was reported in Jackson County. High winds caused some minor damage north of Maquoketa.

Thunderstorms erupted ahead of a warm front as it moved north into Iowa. The storms moved into west central and central Iowa, Hail in excess of two inches in diameter caused damage in Little Sioux in Harrison County. A small tornado touched down in Audubon County west of Audubon. It struck one farm, taking down several trees and destroying the barn. A funnel cloud was also sighted in Mills County, west of Glenwood. There were scattered reports of high winds with some of the storms. In Shelby County, a farm was damaged by high winds in the Portsmouth area. In the later stages of the event, heavy rainfall occurred in Dallas County. Two to three inches of rain fell in under two hours on already saturated ground. Water quickly filled ditches and overtopped roads around the county. Thunderstorms that preceded the main area of activity moved across the Ames area in Story County. Lightning struck a workshop two miles south of Ames setting it ablaze. The shop was destroyed. Later in the morning, the area of thunderstorms moved into east central Iowa. Only one report of severe weather was received as three-quarter inch diameter hail fell southwest of Muscatine.

A cold front began moving into Iowa from the northwest. Copious amounts of moisture was available for this event with precipitable water values around two inches. Thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon hours. By the early evening the storms had formed into a well developed mesoscale convective system. The main feature with the storms was the heavy rainfall, however there was some severe weather associated with the storms during the event. Golf ball-size hail pelted the area around Schleswig in Crawford County. In fact, baseball-size hail to the south of Schleswig caused total crop destruction in the area. The largest hail reported was in Harrison County at Little Sioux. Hail reached three inches in diameter causing considerable crop damage. In Dow City, also in Crawford County, high winds in what appeared to be a microburst struck. A farm was leveled by winds around 85 MPH. High winds were also reported in Carroll County in the city of Carroll. Minor damage occurred in Decatur City in Decatur County during the decaying stages of the system. There were a few tornadoes spawned by the system. They were each quite small and were only on the ground for a short period of time. One tornado touched down in Crawford County south of Vail. The tornado downed several trees and destroyed a few out buildings. Another tornado touched down near Boone in an open field, causing little damage. A similar situation occurred in Greene County west of Jefferson as well as in Chickasaw County north of New Hampton. One of the storms became rather intense and produced a tornado that was on the ground in Dallas County for several miles. Little damage was reported as the tornado passed between several farmsteads. The same storm cluster later produced a funnel cloud over the northeast part of Des Moines. Reports indicated the funnel was very near touching the ground. Other reports of funnel clouds were received from Cherokee County, where four of them were observed west of Cherokee. A few funnel cloud reports were also received from the surrounding counties, but there were no touch downs. Extremely heavy rainfall was reported in Audubon, Crawford, Carroll, and Greene Counties. Damage was very heavy in Crawford County. Initial reports showed that damage in the county was in the $3-4 million range. Story County was also hard hit as 2 1/2 to 5 inches of rain fell across the Squaw Creek basin. Flooding was severe in Ames, with the creek reaching an all time high. Damage to Iowa State University was in the millions of dollars. The Skunk River also rose markedly, causing additional problems, and eventually closing Interstate 35 fora while. The heaviest rainfall was reported around Coon Rapids with 7.83 inches falling in a few hours time. There were numerous reports of three to seven inch rainfall amounts. Manilla reported 7.50 inches of rainfall, with nearly that amount in Denison. Unofficial amounts were higher. In Greene County, the city of Scranton reported 11 inches of rainfall, while ten inches was reported in Carroll County at Willey. In Crawford County, damage from flash flooding was estimated at $15 million. Severe flood damage occurred in 50 homes in Denison and 36 in Dow City. The water rose so quickly that reports indicated that some homes flooded in as little at 11 minutes. Monona County was also hard hit, with rainfall in the four to nine inch range from Onawa east into Harrison County. Damage was extensive in Shelby County where the flood waters washed out several bridges. Highway 59 was under water two miles south of Defiance. Highway 191 was closed between Earling and Panama by flooding from Mosquito Creek. Two hundred and fifty people were forced out of a mobile home park in Harlan, where the water and sewage plant was flooded. Water ran three feet deep in Irwin. Heavy rainfall in excess of three inches fell across much of the north half of the Raccoon River Basin, and extended into the middle Des Moines River Basin. These rains closed numerous roads and washed out bridges in several counties. At one time the Crawford County sheriff reported that nearly all roads in the county were closed by high water. The heavy rainfall set the stage for what was to become the flood of record along the Raccoon and Des Moines River. Flash flooding also occurred east of this area along much of the line of thunderstorms. The flooding extended on a scattered basis all the way to the northeast part of the state. Some of the heavier rains fell in Tama County. Four inches of rain fell resulting in water in the streets of Tama and Chelsea of seven feet in depth.

Southern Iowa was ahead of the cold front in the warm sector. During the evening hours a Derecho formed over southern Nebraska. The Derecho races across southern Nebraska and southern Iowa at 50 to 60 knots. High winds in the 70 to 100 MPH range were reported with the system. As the storms moved into Iowa, a Bow Echo formed on the lead edge. High winds of 90 to 100 MPH downed 13 high tension power line poles in the eastern part of Council Bluffs. Winds of at least 85 MPH ripped into Fremont County, blowing a church off of its foundation in Bartlett. Considerable tree and building structural damage was reported across the southwest quarter of the state. As an example, roof damage was reported to one house and garage with windows blown in at Pilot Grove Park in Montgomery County, with a shed and barn leveled in Page County near Bethesda. There were two injuries as the storms rolled through. One was south of Glenwood in Mills County as a woman sustained minor injuries from flying debris. Another woman was cut by flying glass near Portsmouth as high winds ripped through the area. Other damage in southwest Iowa included the roof being blown off of a house south of Glenwood and another roof taken off of a mobile home hear Hastings. High winds uprooted trees in Red Oak in Montgomery County. Five miles east of Elliot, a house had windows blown out and damage was done to the roof. As the storms moved into Des Moines, high winds blew car windows out on the south side of the city. High winds in Warren county picked up a gravity bin wagon north of Lacona and threw it 50 feet. A pontoon boat was tossed 100 feet by high winds near Seymour. A few tornadoes were reported. One was actually a gustnado in Monroe County. Several roofs were damaged and tree tops were taken off in the town of Albia. Another tornado touched down briefly north of Agency in Wapello County. A metal building was completely flattened. In what turned out to be one of the stronger tornadoes, a touchdown was reported in the Portsmouth area. Two houses were damaged extensively. In addition, a mobile home was overturned with the roof taken off of another building. A horse trailer was picked up and carried for 250 feet. Rainfall was heavy with the Derecho, but with the speed of movement the amounts were generally less than an inch. Late in the severe weather episode, general river flooding began. The Boyer River flooded through Harrison County from heavy upstream rains. Homes, businesses, and croplands were flooded including areas around Woodbine and Missouri Valley. Seventy five to 80 homes were flooded in Missouri Valley where water was 3 to 4 feet deep in places. The Missouri River also flooded the Willow Creek Area. The West Nishnabotna River flooded through Pottawattamie County. About 50 people were evacuated in Avoca where water flooded the town to the highest levels since 1947. Interstate 80 was closed in the area for a time on the 9th after water swept a number of cars off the roadway. Downstream, record flooding occurred around the Hancock area where the park was heavily damaged. The crest rolled into the Oakland area early on the 10th, overflowing sand bags and flooding widespread areas of the town. Numerous roads were flooded and bridges damaged. Crop damage was heavy. The Missouri River also overflowed, forcing evacuations at Goose Haven and Honey Creek. In Mills and Fremont Counties, the West Nishnabotna River flooded croplands and roads throughout the area, damaging some bridges. Some overflows affected the area around Hastings.

The crest rolled into the Oakland area early on the 10th, overflowing sand bags and flooding widespread areas of the town. Numerous roads were flooded and bridges damaged. Crop damage was heavy. The Missouri River also overflowed, forcing evacuations at Goose Haven and Honey Creek. In Mills and Fremont Counties, the West Nishnabotna River flooded croplands and roads throughout the area, damaging some bridges. Some overflows affected the area around Hastings.

Thunderstorms fired up across northern Iowa in a very moist and unstable atmosphere. They were ahead of an approaching cold front. The storms fired during the early afternoon hours. They tracked across northern Iowa into the east-central counties. A few tornadoes were spawned by the stronger storms. One touched down briefly in Cerro Gordo County. The second touched down in Floyd County. This tornado was on the ground for about 12 mifes and caused damage to a few farmsteads. For the most part the storms caused high winds, at times gusting to around 80 MPH. Winds gusted to 80 MPH in Ogden, in Boone County. Numerous reports of trees and power lines being downed by the high winds were received. Early in the storms development, large hail was reported in northwest Iowa. Baseball and larger size hail fell in Lyon and Sioux Counties with a swath of 90% crop damage from northwest to southeast of Boydon. All of the windows on the north side of the houses in Boydon were broken by the hail. Other reports of hail were received after these initial reports. Most of the hail was pea to marble-size. Three-quarter inch diameter hail fell in Winneshiek County at Decorah, while the largest hail report was in Webster County. Callender reported golf ball to softball-size hail briefly. Crops were destroyed and leaves stripped off of trees in the area. The combination of the hail and three inches of rainfall caused large drifts of hail. High winds resulted in an injury in Floyd County. An 11 year old was injured at a campground as a tree branch fell on his leg. In Palo Alto County, lightning struck a golf cart shed at a local golf course. It started a fire that destroyed the shed and several carts.

The cold front mentioned in the previous days narrative continued to progress slowly into the state. The airmass was somewhat drier on the 18th compared to the 19th. A narrow line of showers and thunderstorms developed from Carroll County east to Marshall County. There were numerous reports of funnel clouds along this line. In many ways, there were more like cold air funnels than true funnels typically associated with severe thunderstorms. The tops of the thunderstorms were not very high. Two brief touch downs were reported. One was on the east side of Marshalltown. The tornado touched down briefly and caused only minor damage. The second touchdown was in Jasper County east of Prairie City. The tornado touched down briefly in a field there.

The synoptic situation was set up a little differently than that of the past several days. The warm front had moved north into Iowa, however several old outflow boundaries remained from the past days convection. There were three main differences in the pattern on this day as compared with the previous several. The first was that a strong low level jet became established during the evening. What was on the order of 30 kts by late afternoon increased to 50 to 60 kts during the evening. This was stronger than the low level jet of the past several days. A cold front was approaching, which also aided in the formation of convection. The third factor was a strong short wave, or upper air disturbance, approaching the area. These factors combined to set of explosive thunderstorm development during the late afternoon hours into the evening. The storms first fired up over southeast Nebraska. The storm cluster expanded into a mesoscale convective complex in just three hours time as the low level jet pushed a pool of 75 to 80 degree dew point temperatures into the region. The storms produced copious rainfall over parts of Nebraska. During the early evening a strong line developed on the lead edge of the complex. This line advanced into lowa at nearly 50 kts. This spared lowa of what could have been a flooding/flash flooding event of historical proportions. The speed of movement kept precipitation amounts under two inches in most areas. Heavy rainfall of two inches in a 30 minute time me period was reported in Council Bluffs area. Streets were flooded with numerous intersections under water. A theater was damaged when flood waters crept in. About two feet of water covered the theater's parking lot. The storm complex was tornadic as it moved across southeast Nebraska. Two tornadoes were spawned in southwest Iowa. The first straddled the Mills and Fremont County line south of Glenwood. It was preceded by two funnel cloud reports in Fremont County about 20 minutes prior to touchdown. The tornado damaged trees and caused considerable damage to a mobile home east of Bartlett. The main feature with the storms was high winds. A few funnel clouds were reported over southwest Iowa during the early stages of the event. They were reported in both Page and Adams Counties. A small tornado touched down briefly in the town of Corning about an hour before. The funnel cloud came from a secondary storm that developed. The storms did produce some small hail in the Moville area of Woodbury County. Reports of winds of 70 MPH or more were numerous. Tree and power line damage was quite widespread. In Woodbury County northwest of Climbing Hill, high winds downed power lines and damaged a hog shed on one farm. Sheet metal was strewn across the road there. High winds struck southeast of the town of Treynor in Pottawattamie County. The 75 MPH winds downed several barns and damaged outbuildings in the area. Two farms south of Walnut sustained heavy damage from the thunderstorm winds. A roof was lifted off one farmhouse. A large metal storage shed was twisted and smashed. A barn was destroyed and several grain bins were lifted. The storms high winds downed a barn south of Creston, in Union County. Considerable damage was reported in Guthrie County. A lot of trees were downed, the roof was taken off of one house, part of the roof on the 4H building, and the roof of the ready mix plant were all taken off in Guthrie Center. A small camper was moved across a parking lot there as well. Needless to say, considerable damage was also done to power lines in the area. As one of the stronger storms moved across the Des Moines Airport, very high winds were recorded. An apparent microburst occurred along with the passage of the gust front. In actuality, the highest winds occurred after the first thunderstorms moved over the airport. An intense storm just to the south of the airport resulted in wind gusts of 83 MPH at the airport. The Air Traffic Control Tower recorded a sustained 89 MPH wind for a period of several minutes. The storms moved east and produced 70 MPH winds in northern Warren County at Carlisle. Significant tree and power line damage was reported in the area. Another isolated wind event occurred in Franklin County at Hampton. Roof damage was reported from several buildings at the Franklin County Fairgrounds, caused by high winds. After midnight, a small cluster of storms formed in southwest Iowa. They became severe and produced high winds in Union County in the Creston area. The area southwest of Creston was hardest hit when high winds leveled a block wide area. Once again, this appeared to be a microburst and not a tornado in spite of the fact that the radar echo tops were in excess of 70,000 feet. The storm continued to move east and produced high winds in Clarke County. Winds downed several trees and some power lines in Osceola. All of the storms produced torrential rains. Flash flooding was minimal due to the speed of movement, however there were some local problems mainly in urban areas. The storms moved east during the night and resulted in damage as they moved through Cedar County. An outbuilding was moved off of its foundation west of Lowden. North of Lowden, shingles were blown off of a house and stuck into the screen in front of a picture window. Several trees were downed in the area as well.

A tornado touched down on the north side of Mackinac Island. The tornado path was from British Landing on the northwest side of the island northeast to the other side of the island near Scotts Shore road. Aerial survey indicated total destruction of trees in some areas and other areas where the tops of the trees were destroyed. Less than 50 percent of the path had destruction. Ground survey indicated trees in some areas had fallen down in different directions. Some trees were also uprooted.

A tornado touched down on the west side of Mackinaw Island. The tornado path was in a north to south line mostly near the dirt road called Forest Way. The path extended from 3/4 mile south of British Landing to 1/4 mile south of British Landing. Some trees were uprooted and some were broken and twisted along the path. Buildings in this area has some damage to roofs due to fallen trees. Trees up to 25 inches in diameter were destroyed. Only about 10 percent of the path had destruction. One minor injury was reported from flying glass due to the wind. Power was out in the affected areas for 14 to 16 hours.

A mobile home was lifted off its foundation and dropped to the ground. It was tied down with steel cables which prevented it from flipping over. All the windows were blown out of the mobile home. A barn south of the mobile home was totally destroyed and one horse was killed. Both the owner of the mobile home and fire officials enroute to the scene reported seeing a funnel cloud in the vicinity of the damage. There was other damage to trees and wires, and another barn had part of its roof removed.

A small, weak tornado touched down three miles north of Gaylord and moved northeast across mostly wooded areas of Otsego county for nearly 12 miles, passing to the south and east of the village of Vanderbilt, The tornado did mainly FO damage through most of its track, but strengthened briefly to F1 intensity near the intersection of Old Vanderbilt Road and Whitehouse Trail, where it moved one very old cottage off its foundation and damaged another, destroyed a pole, barn and did minor damage to a mobile home, then the tornado did mainly roof damage to two homes and a garage. As the tornado lifted, it sucked screens out of buildings at Camp Vanderbilt.

A small tornado touched down occasionally as it tracked eastward over a three and a half mile path from three miles northwest of Middleville to about one mile northeast of Middleville. Damage was slight and there was no injuries. Basement windows were blown out, and an eight foot Dutch windmill was blown away. There was some damage to a wheat field and straw was blown into the bark of trees. There were several other sightings of funnel clouds across northern Barry County.

Severe thunderstorms hit southern Wisconsin with a variety of weather including one tornado, violent Thunderstorm wind to 66 mph and heavy rain which caused extensive flash flooding in many counties. The tornado set down on a farm one mile west of Genoa City in Walworth County moving a silo off its foundation and damaging a horse barn and 25 trees. Violent thunderstorms winds knocked down numerous trees and power lines as well as blowing down grain bins in Campbellsport (Fond du Lac County), a barn in Whitelaw (Manitowoc County) and causing roof damage in Two Rivers (Manitowoc County). Rainfall amounts of three to seven inches allowed the Black Earth Creek to overflow its banks, flooding the towns of Mazomanie (Dane County) and Black Earth (Dane County). The Little Platte river flooded parts of Platteville (Grant County). Bonner Creek overflowed flooding part of the town of Belmont (Lafayette yette County) including a lumberyard. Water poured out of Tarrant Lake and rushed into Cambria (Columbia County) flooding a factory, several businesses, roads and homes. Apple Creek near DePere (Brown County) spilled over its banks flooding a campground. In Fond du Lac (Fond du Lac County) the Fond du Lac River flooded nine homes after leaving its banks. Numerous highways and secondary roads were washed out or flooded for extended periods of time in other counties.

A small tornado set down one mile east of Beetown (Grant County) damaging a mobile home,car,pole shed and trees. Another tornado struck three miles north of Platteville (Grant County) damaging three houses,two barns and two sheds along with many trees. Rainfall of more than four inches in one hour overflowed a storm ditch in Glenhaven (Grant County) sending a five foot wall of water through the town. A line of severe thunderstorms swept across southern Wisconsin accompanied by one tornado, winds gusting up to 70 mph and hail up to nickel-size. Three golfers were injured when struck by a lightning bolt near Holmen (LaCrosse County). A tornado briefly set down near the northeast shore of Lake Eau Claire (Eau Claire County) and damaged 12 trees. Violent Thunderstorm wind pushed a mobile home off its foundation near Cataract (Monroe County), damaged 12 homes and five cars in Sun Prairie (Dane County) and caused a variety of damage to 13 planes and a small building at the EAA Fly-In at Oshkosh (Winnebago County). Otherwise damage was confined to trees and power lines.
A public report of a tornado north of Torrington for several minutes with no damage or injuries.
No damage or injuries from a brief tornado near Esterbrook.
The public reported a tornado in open country north of Gillette with no damage or injuries.
